minutes.headline: Board of Health voted to approve a bedroom-expansion building permit on condition of a three-bedroom deed restriction.
minutes.summary: A short remote meeting whose only substantive item was a property owner's request to convert a room into a larger bedroom while staying at three bedrooms. what_happened.line: The Board of Health approved a building permit for a bedroom expansion on condition that a three-bedroom deed restriction is recorded; Evan Waters abstained.
The owner will get help from the administrative assistant with the deed restriction form, which must be signed, notarized and recorded before the permit is signed off.
A second agenda item was postponed because the applicant had not supplied the requested current water test; minutes are to be approved at the next meeting.
A former board member asked in public comment whether the property could tie into municipal sewer, noting sewer is available at the street.

why_it_matters: Bedroom count is what a septic system is sized and permitted for, so a deed restriction at three bedrooms keeps a larger room from changing the wastewater capacity the property is approved for, and it stays with the property for later owners.
The sewer question was raised in comment and not decided; whether the property could connect to municipal sewer instead of a compliant septic system is open on this record.
watch_next: Recording of the deed restriction on the property, which the minutes say must happen before the permit is signed off.
The postponed second agenda item, which waits on the applicant supplying a current water test, and the approval of these minutes at the next meeting.
